ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows triangle PQR, with base PQ horizontal, side QR vertical, and a right-angle mark at Q, so ∠PQR is a right angle. Point S is on hypotenuse PR, and the hypotenuse is divided into two segments, PS=2 and SR=4. Segment QS connects from Q to S, and there is a right-angle mark at S, indicating that QS is perpendicular to PR. The unknown x is marked on the vertical side QR. Reasoning: Because PQR is a right triangle, and S is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the right-angle vertex Q to the hypotenuse PR, the right-triangle hypotenuse projection theorem can be used. The hypotenuse PR=PS+SR=2+4=6. The hypotenuse projection of side QR is SR=4 adjacent to R, therefore QR^2=PR·SR=6·4=24. Thus x=QR=√24=2√6.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a right triangle PQR with right angle at Q. Point S lies on hypotenuse PR, with PS=2 and SR=4, so PR=6. The segment QS is drawn perpendicular to PR, making S the foot of the altitude from the right angle to the hypotenuse. The unknown x labels leg QR. Apply the right-triangle altitude/projection theorem: each leg squared equals the hypotenuse times the adjacent hypotenuse segment. Since QR is adjacent to segment SR, compute x^2=PR·SR=6·4=24, so x=2√6.
